hints: When the tube changed temperature, did the brown get stronger or weaker?

Le Chatelier's principle: a balanced reaction shifts to push back against a change. Add heat, and it shifts the way that soaks heat up, like a sponge. Splitting colourless N₂O₄ into brown NO₂ takes in heat. So heating makes the gas browner.
Try the ice bath at 0 °C. Cooling favours the direction that gives out heat. Will the gas get darker or paler?
